title: config Module
content_markdown: The _config_ module enables dynamic, runtime configuration of OpenSIPS parameters by loading them from persistent storage at startup and exposing them to the script level via the [$config(...)](#pv_config "1.4.1.�$config(name)") pseudo-variable.
overview: The _config_ module enables dynamic, runtime configuration of OpenSIPS parameters by loading them from persistent storage at startup and exposing them to the script level via the [$config(...)](#pv_config "1.4.1.�$config(name)") pseudo-variable.
how_it_works:
All configuration variables are stored in OpenSIPS' internal cache, allowing fast access during SIP processing to maintain high performance. The cache can be updated in three ways:

* _Script_ – Assigning a value to the [$config(...)](#pv_config "1.4.1.�$config(name)") pseudo-variable updates the in-memory cache, but this change is not persisted to the database.
* _MI Commands_ – Using [config_push](#mi_config_push "1.5.3.�config_push") or [config_push_bulk](#mi_config_push_bulk "1.5.4.�config_push_bulk") updates one or more variables in the runtime cache. These updates are also not saved to the database.
* _Database_ – Manually modifying values in the database, then triggering the [config_reload](#mi_config_reload "1.5.1.�config_reload") command, will refresh the in-memory cache with updated values from the database.

### 1.1.1.�Restart Persistent Memory

By default, the configuration cache is initialized at startup by reading from the database and persists only during the runtime. Any temporary changes made through the script or MI commands that are not explicitly flushed to the database using the [config_flush](#mi_config_flush "1.5.5.�config_flush") command will be lost after a restart.

In such cases, restart persistent memory becomes useful. When enabled via the [enable_restart_persistency](#param_enable_rpm "1.3.6.�enable_restart_persistency (integer)") parameter, OpenSIPS no longer loads configuration values from the database on startup. Instead, it restores the previously saved in-memory cache, preserving runtime changes across restarts.

If needed, you can still manually re-initialize the cache from the database by running the [config_reload](#mi_config_reload "1.5.1.�config_reload") MI command.

dependencies_required.name: database module
dependencies_required.reason: needed to read the initial cache

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: Database URL used to load the initial configuration values, and flush them at runtime using the config_flush MI command.

exported_parameters.name: table_name
exported_parameters.description: Name of the table where configuration entries are stored.

exported_parameters.name: name_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the column storing configuration variable names.

exported_parameters.name: value_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the column storing configuration variable values.

exported_parameters.name: description_column
exported_parameters.description: Name of the column storing variable descriptions.

exported_parameters.name: enable_restart_persistency
exported_parameters.description: Enables restart persistency. Check the Restart Persistent Memory for more information.

exported_parameters.name: hash_size
exported_parameters.description: Size of the internal hash table used to store config variables. Must be a power of 2 number, otherwise its value will be rounded to the closest value of 2 smaller than the provided value.

exported_mi_functions.name: config_reload
exported_mi_functions.description: Reloads all configuration variables from the database.

examples.code:
## reload configuration cache from the database
		opensips-mi config_reload
examples.description: reload configuration cache from the database

exported_mi_functions.name: config_list

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: If provided and different than 0, it returns an array containing the description of the values as well.

return_value.description: Array containing the description of the values as well (if description parameter provided).

exported_mi_functions.description: Lists all config variables currently loaded in cache, printing temporary values as well. If the optional _description_ parameter is provided and different than _0_, it returns an array containing the description of the values as well.

examples.code:
## list all configuration cache
		opensips-mi config_list

exported_mi_functions.name: config_push

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: the description of the variable; if missing the description is inheritted, or a null value is used if the variable is new.

exported_mi_functions.description: Temporarily pushes a single configuration variable.

examples.code:
## push temporarily debug_mode configuration value
		opensips-mi config_push debug_mode 1 "Enable Debug mode"

exported_mi_functions.name: config_push_bulk

parameters.name: configs
parameters.description: a JSON array containing a set of variables to be pushed. Each variable should be described as a JSON object with the following keys: name (string), value (string or null), description (string, optional).

return_value.description: The number of values successfully pushed.

exported_mi_functions.description: Pushes multiple temporarily configuration variables in memory.

examples.code:
## push bulk temporarily values to the config cache
		opensips-mi config_push_bulk -j '\[\[{"name":"debug_mode","value":"1"},{"name":"debug_level","value":"5"}\]\]'
examples.description: push bulk temporarily values to the config cache

exported_mi_functions.name: config_flush

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: if present, flushes only a specific config variable in database, otherwise the entire cache.

return_value.description: The number of values successfully flushed.

exported_mi_functions.description: Flushes the variables from the memory to the database.

examples.code:
## Flush config variables to the database
		opensips-mi config_flush
examples.description: Flush config variables to the database

exported_pseudo_variables.description: Returns the value of the given config variable by name. Can also be used for temporarily changing the value.

exported_pseudo_variables.name: $config.description(name)
